text: Now that you have your degree, what feels missing the most?

options.text: I need a broader view — management, strategy, and leadership.
I want to go deeper into my technical field through advanced study.
I want to serve my country through a government role.
I want to start building something of my own right now.

text: What kind of problem gets you most energized?

options.text: Organizational inefficiency — teams that underperform or strategies that fail.
Technical puzzles — unsolved engineering or computing challenges.
Social injustice — corruption, inequality, or policy failures.
Financial complexity — markets, risk, valuations, or tax structures.

text: If you could shadow a professional for one month, who would it be?

options.text: A CEO or Strategy Consultant at a top firm.
A Senior Engineer at ISRO, Google DeepMind, or a top R&D lab.
An IAS / IPS officer managing a district.
A Supreme Court advocate or High Court judge.

text: How do you feel about spending 2–3 more years in studying?

options.text: Fine — but I want an MBA that has direct ROI in salary and promotions.
I love studying — I want a M.Tech or MS that sharpens my technical edge.
I'm okay with years of preparation if it leads to a prestigious government role.
I'd rather work and learn on the job — I want to start earning now.

text: Where do you see yourself working in 5 years?

options.text: As a manager or team lead in a multinational company or consulting firm.
As a specialist engineer, data scientist, or researcher at a top tech company.
As a government officer (IAS, IPS, IFS) or in public sector leadership.
Running my own startup or freelancing independently.

text: Which of these tasks do you enjoy most during your graduation?

options.text: Group projects, presentations, leading teams, and strategy discussions.
Coding assignments, lab experiments, and thesis writing.
Reading case studies, writing essays on policy or law.
Financial modelling, case competitions, and market analysis.

text: Which magazine or news section do you enjoy reading most?

options.text: Business Today, Forbes, Harvard Business Review.
IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Science Daily, Nature.
The Hindu's opinion, Frontline, or policy briefs.
Economic Times, Mint, or CFA Institute publications.

text: What is your biggest strength that you want a career to reward?

options.text: People management, negotiation, and strategic thinking.
Deep domain expertise, precision, and analytical problem-solving.
Communication, advocacy, and the ability to influence others.
Empathy, community orientation, and grassroots impact.

text: How important is financial earning to you right now?

options.text: Very important — I want a top salary package within 2–3 years.
Important — I want a good salary but am willing to invest 3 years in M.Tech / MS.
Moderate — government jobs offer stability which matters more than salary.
I'm willing to earn less now if I'm building something meaningful.

text: If you were to write a paper or report, what topic would you choose?

options.text: Market entry strategies for a D2C startup in Tier-2 Indian cities.
Optimizing deep learning models for edge computing devices.
Reforming India's judicial backlog and access to legal aid.
How microfinance can empower women in rural Rajasthan.

text: What kind of feedback energizes you most?

options.text: "Your strategy was brilliant and your team executed perfectly."
"Your algorithm is 40% more efficient than anything published before."
"Your argument won the case / your policy report was cited."
"Your work changed the lives of 500 families in that village."

text: Which statement best describes your relationship with risk?

options.text: I take calculated risks with strong data and planning to back me up.
I prefer methodical research before taking any steps.
I prefer the structured, predictable path of government or law.
I thrive on uncertainty — building from scratch is exciting to me.

text: How do you feel about relocating abroad for work or study?

options.text: Yes — I want an MBA from a global B-school and an international career.
Yes — I want an MS from MIT, Stanford, or a top European university.
No — I want to serve India; relocation abroad doesn't appeal to me.
Open to it — but only if my business or creative work demands it.

text: Which certification or exam would you most seriously consider?

options.text: CAT / GMAT for MBA admission.
GATE for M.Tech / PSU jobs.
UPSC Civil Services / State PSC.
CFA / FRM / CA Final for finance.

text: If all careers paid equally well, which would you genuinely pursue?

options.text: Building and leading organizations — a CEO or management consultant.
Inventing the next breakthrough in science or technology.
Serving in IAS/IPS or practicing constitutional law.
Creating art, media, or social change that impacts millions.

text: Now that you hold a postgraduate degree, what pulls you forward?

options.text: The urge to discover something no one has found yet — research excites me.
I want to apply my knowledge in a top corporate role with real impact.
I want to build something of my own using my advanced expertise.
I want to shape the minds of the next generation as a professor or trainer.

Internships, live projects, and industry interactions.
Strategy simulations, consulting case competitions, and presentations.
Policy debates, seminars, and engaging with social or governance issues.

text: Which of these is your biggest professional strength today?

options.text: Deep domain expertise that very few people in the country possess.
The ability to manage teams, projects, and stakeholders at scale.
Pattern recognition and the ability to solve complex business problems.
Communication, simplifying complexity, and inspiring others.

text: How do you feel about 3–5 more years of academic life for a PhD?

options.text: Excited — I want to contribute original knowledge to my field.
Not for me — I'd rather apply knowledge in the real world.
I'd consider it only if it directly helps my business or consultancy.
I'd consider it if it leads to a tenured professorship I'm proud of.

text: How do you prefer to make decisions?

options.text: Based on rigorous data analysis, peer-reviewed evidence, and experimentation.
Based on business KPIs, ROI projections, and team consensus.
Based on market gaps, gut instinct validated by quick experiments.
Based on policy frameworks, ethical principles, and societal impact.

options.text: Being published in top journals and cited by peers worldwide.
A Director / VP title and a high-compensation package at a top firm.

Senior Manager / Director / VP at a Fortune 500 company.
Founder / Co-founder of a high-growth startup.
Independent Consultant / Subject Matter Expert / Freelancer.

options.text: I want flexibility — research or academia gives me schedule control.
I'm okay with demanding hours if it leads to career advancement fast.
Completely unpredictable — I want to build something and I accept that chaos.
I want complete control — I'll set my own hours as a consultant or freelancer.

text: Which sector would you most like to influence through your career?

options.text: Science, technology, or academia — knowledge creation.
Business, finance, or industry — economic value creation.
Governance, public policy, or social development.

It's part of the job — I can do it but it's not my primary strength.
I love it — pitching ideas and winning clients energizes me.
I'd rather influence through policy papers and public speaking.

text: What is the main reason you want to switch careers?

options.text: My current work feels repetitive — I want intellectually stimulating challenges.
I want higher financial rewards and faster growth.
I want to do work that feels meaningful and socially impactful.

Communication, persuasion, and stakeholder management.

"Build and manage brand campaigns that reach 10 million users."
"Advise Fortune 500 companies on their 5-year growth strategy."
"Build a financial model to evaluate an acquisition worth ₹200 crore."

text: How comfortable are you with learning new technical skills from scratch?

Comfortable — I can learn financial tools and market analysis.
Moderate — I prefer applying skills, not learning deeply technical ones.
I prefer creative or human-centric skills — tools are secondary.

options.text: Independent deep work — solving complex problems alone.
Collaborative — constantly working with people, teams, and clients.
Entrepreneurial — building things, taking risks, experimenting fast.
Community-driven — working with beneficiaries, communities, or patients.

options.text: Losing the technical depth I've built over years.
Taking a salary cut during the transition period.
Starting over and being seen as a junior again.
Losing creative freedom in a structured corporate environment.

options.text: Working on cutting-edge AI, product, or cloud projects.
Running my own consultancy with high-value corporate clients.
Leading a marketing or brand team at a company I admire.
Running my own business or working as a full-time freelancer.

options.text: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, or Cloud Computing.
Investment Banking, Private Equity, or Fintech.
UX/UI Design, Motion Graphics, or Content Creation.
Healthcare delivery, MedTech innovation, or mental health services.

options.text: Fully willing — I'll upskill and take an entry-level role in tech.
Willing — but I need to see a clear ROI within 12 months.
Minimally — I need to freelance or consult while transitioning.
Not willing — I want a lateral move that keeps my current salary.

text: Which describes how you make your best contribution at work?

options.text: By building systems, automating processes, and writing code.
By persuading stakeholders and crafting compelling narratives.
By developing people, resolving conflicts, and building culture.
By creating visually powerful experiences and original content.

text: What is your strongest motivation for starting a business?

options.text: I have a technology idea that can scale to millions of users.
I want to sell a product I believe in — build a brand.
I want to offer a specialized service and be my own boss.
I want to solve a social problem and create sustainable impact.

text: How do you feel about raising external funding (VC / Angel investment)?

options.text: I'd actively seek it — VCs bring capital AND connections for tech growth.
I'd prefer bootstrapping — I want full control and no equity dilution.
I'd consider grants or impact investors for a social venture.
I'd get a bank loan — I'm building a traditional, profitable business.

text: Which of these best describes your idea of success in 5 years?

options.text: A 100-person company with Series B funding and a product used globally.
A profitable brand with ₹10 crore revenue selling on Amazon and D2C.
A premium consulting or agency with 50 high-paying clients.
1 million subscribers / followers and a passive income of ₹3 LPM.

text: What is your core skill that you'd build a business around?

options.text: Coding, product development, and tech architecture.
Marketing, storytelling, brand building, and aesthetics.
Domain expertise — I'm exceptionally good at one professional skill.
Community building, empathy, and grassroots mobilization.

text: How do you feel about the uncertainty and risk of starting from zero?

options.text: I thrive on it — uncertainty is where opportunity lives.
I'm okay with calculated risk — I'll validate before I commit.
I prefer lower risk — I'll follow a proven model (franchise / agency).
I want sustainable impact — I can tolerate risk if the cause is worth it.

text: What is your biggest challenge in starting a business right now?

options.text: Finding technical co-founders and building the MVP.
Getting the first 100 customers and cracking marketing.
Landing the first paying client for my skills or service.
Convincing investors or donors that my social idea is viable.

A premium physical product with a strong emotional brand story.
Online courses or coaching that transform careers.
A service that helps other businesses grow — marketing, HR, or operations.

Job security, a stable salary, and a comfortable retirement.
Serving the nation in a disciplined, action-oriented environment.
Passing on knowledge — I want to be a respected teacher or professor.

Physics, Mathematics, or Engineering subjects.
